reason: The wound needs its broken fragments cleared before new tissue can bridge the gap. White blood cells are pictured surrounding those fragments.
expectation: I expect the white blood cells to clear debris from the wound while the clot remains in place.

alternatives.reason: A new blood supply also supports repair, but clearing the wound seems like a useful first step.

effect: The fragments are cleared and the clot remains. The open slots show that the wound still needs a supply, surface and support.
reaction: It is satisfying to see the debris cleared without disturbing the clot.
reason: The picture shows wound messengers reaching a nearby vessel and a new branch growing, which should help rebuild the blood supply.
expectation: I expect a new blood-vessel branch to grow toward the wound, though I don't know exactly how the messengers cause it.

alternatives.reason: Building supporting fibres also helps repair, but I want to prepare the blood supply first.

effect: The messengers produced a capillary sprout, which can now be added to the cleared wound.
reaction: The new branch makes the blood-supply step easier to picture.
reason: I'll fit the sprout into the wound to continue rebuilding its blood supply.
expectation: I expect the new vessel branch to become part of the wound's developing blood supply.

alternatives.reason: Supporting fibres are also needed, but I want to finish placing the vessel first.

effect: The new branch connects to another vessel, allowing blood and materials to reach nearby cells. The wound still needs surface and support.
reaction: Seeing the branch become a working route makes its purpose clear.
reason: The support-building cells need amino acids to make the fibres that will help rebuild the wound.
expectation: I expect the cells to produce supporting protein fibres that can be added to the wound.

alternatives.reason: Preparing replacement surface cells also matters, but I'll build the support first.

effect: The cells made new protein fibres, but the deeper gap remains open until they are fitted into the wound.
reaction: The outline makes it clear where the new fibres belong.
reason: I'll add the fibres to help rebuild support across the gap.
expectation: I expect the fibres to join the existing tissue and fill the support slot, though the surface will still need repair.

alternatives.reason: Preparing surface cells is also needed, but I'll place the fibres first.

effect: The fibres now support part of the deeper wound, and the game says the temporary clot must eventually be cleared.
reaction: The repair is coming together, though the surface is still open.
reason: This is the only offered combination. The pictured oxygen and nutrients should help the edge cells grow and close the surface.
expectation: I expect the skin cells to produce replacement cells for the wound surface.

effect: New skin cells are ready at the wound edge, but the surface gap remains open.
reaction: The outline makes their next placement clear.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and it should help close the skin surface.
expectation: I expect the new cells to spread across the gap and close the surface; the temporary clot may still need clearing.

effect: The new cells closed the surface, but the tissue underneath is still strengthening and the temporary clot remains.
reaction: Closing the visible gap feels like clear progress.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and the enzymes are pictured cutting clot threads, matching the remaining goal.
expectation: I expect the enzymes to break down the temporary clot while the repaired skin remains in place.

effect: Most clot threads are gone, while the new fibres and blood vessels remain. The skin is closed, but the scar will keep changing.
reaction: The small scar makes the repair feel more realistic than an instantly perfect result.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the capillary sprout was most worthwhile: seeing blood flow through the joined vessels made the new supply's purpose clear.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making and then placing the new skin cells felt a little repetitive, especially with only one combination offered each time.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the clot was temporary and that a scar remained after most of its threads were cleared.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt purposeless, though I followed the pictured pairing for wound messengers and the capillary without understanding exactly how the messengers cause a branch to grow.

continue.text: I would probably continue for another chapter: seeing separate repairs come together into a working blood supply and closed surface was satisfying, although some placements were predictable.
